name: archify
one_liner: Exports architecture and data-flow diagrams as self-contained HTML.

text.why: Architecture drawings go stale quickly, and every correction means opening the drawing tool again. archify comes as a skill for coding agents, so architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow and lifecycle diagrams get produced next to the code. The output is a single self-contained HTML file you can open or export as is. Published under MIT.
text.take: Letting the agent draw and validate diagrams next to the code is what keeps them from going stale.
build: Onboarding-document diagrams that explain the repository layout
A one-page system flow diagram for a client proposal
An architecture page redrawn with every release

who.situation: needs a system flow diagram for a proposal
shows architecture before and after a PR

start.text: Describe the system in the agent chat and ask Archify to draw it

caveat: Needs an agent host (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) plus Node.js
Sends an update-check request by default; an env var disables it
Mermaid import and WYSIWYG editing are stated as out of scope

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.

notes: This file was produced by the same build, from the same data, as the tesign.com item page. The text is editorial; the numbers are stored observations.
